department_text: course-list 12 EWRT - English Writing Courses 0 0 EWRT - English Writing Courses EWRT - English Writing Courses Specific courses that were formerly offered under EWRT are now listed under ENGL. They have been renumbered according to the Common Course Numbering System. (Visit deanza.edu/register/course-numbers to learn more about the new course IDs.) Some courses in the English/Writing Department are designed for students with a recommended level of skills and knowledge. De Anza utilizes a variety of assessment methods, including placement tests, high school transcripts, and high school GPA, to place students in the most suitable course sequence for their success. Students who are unsure of their placement should contact the Assessment Center for guidance. courses.title: Introduction to Fundamentals of Writing, Reading, and College Preparation
courses.description: This course introduces students to major conventions of college-level Standard English writing. The course aids in students' development of basic skills in the reading and writing processes. The course includes a practice of focused and purposeful writing in several formats to diverse audiences with a variety of sentence structures responding to, engaging with, and/or inspired by written or visual texts. This course introduces students to college preparation, including navigating studenthood, campus resources, and future success.

courses.title: Professional Writing in the Workplace
courses.description: This course will develop professional writing skills for for-profit as well as nonprofit professional, technical, and science industry and career fields, including but not limited to Automotive Technology, Design and Manufacturing Technology, and Health Care. Students will analyze professional writing templates and examples, and practice composing and editing various forms of professional writing.

metadata.Limitation(s) on Enrollment - Other: Admission to a California Community College Baccalaureate program.
metadata.Student Learning Outcomes: Practice professional writing as a multi-step process, including planning and revising, with attention to effectively and competently communicating with varying purposes, audiences, and rhetorical strategies Identify and apply major technical and stylistic elements of professional writing.
